notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 03/11/2025
Patient: Russel Bernier, 71-year-old male

Summary:
Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 03/11/2025. The study evaluated sleep architecture, respiratory events, and oxygen saturation.

Findings:
Sleep stages were adequately recorded with normal distribution of REM and non-REM sleep. Respiratory events were noted throughout the night. Central and mixed apneas comprised 18% of all events. Oxygen saturation remained stable with occasional mild desaturations corresponding to respiratory events.

Conclusion:
The polysomnography indicates the presence of central and mixed apneas as a significant portion of respiratory events. Further clinical correlation and management recommendations will be provided based on these findings.

Signed,
Sleep Medicine Physician

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/09/2026
Patient: Russel Bernier, 72-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Bernier presents for follow-up regarding his sleep apnea treatment. He has been using CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 33.3 kg/m2.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.0 hours per night on 31% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative treatment options for sleep-disordered breathing, including positional therapy and oral appliance therapy. Continue to monitor symptoms and reassess treatment efficacy at follow-up visits. Provide education and support to optimize sleep hygiene and overall health.

Follow-up:
Schedule return visit in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.
